summary:
Radar Rhythm – Cloud-Piercing Satellite Radar Intelligence for Floods, Farms, and Faults

Radar Rhythm is an innovative, interactive Earth observation platform that uses NASA-ISRO NISAR satellite radar technology to monitor and visualize changes on Earth's surface. Unlike traditional optical satellites, which struggle with dense cloud cover and nighttime conditions, Radar Rhythm uses advanced L-band radar data to observe Earth's surface even during monsoons and challenging weather conditions.

The platform transforms complex satellite data into meaningful visual insights through interactive 3D Earth visualization, radar comparison maps, orbital timelines, and AI-powered explanations. It helps users understand floods, agricultural conditions, ground displacement, and environmental changes across different geographical regions.

The project demonstrates real-world applications of satellite technology through study areas in Maharashtra, Northeast India, and Japan.

Team Leader: Aman Kawale

Team Members: Aman Kawale, Vedant Jaiswal, Kalash Wasad, Humaira Khan, and Asawari Dhawad.
details: Radar Rhythm integrates NASA-ISRO NISAR satellite data with interactive geospatial visualization to monitor Earth's changing surface. It uses GCOV radar data to identify water bodies, flooding, and agricultural patterns, while GUNW data helps visualize ground movement and displacement. The platform features an interactive 3D globe, satellite radar comparison, four-pass orbital timeline, telemetry analytics, and AI-powered physical explanations in English, Hindi, and Marathi. It also incorporates NASA POWER weather data and NASA EONET environmental hazard information. With dedicated study areas covering Maharashtra, Northeast India, and Japan, Radar Rhythm makes complex satellite observations accessible, understandable, and useful for real-world applications.
